Hello, all!

I'm Nerdspartan. I've been interested in SCP since the day I first saw Youtube videos of people playing SCP-087, and later SCP:Containment Breach. Recently, I've stumbled upon the SCP narrative channel TheVolgun, which made me come back to the Foundation.

I love the SCP way of depicting horror in an apathetic and scientific fashion, and I wondered if I could write my own SCPs eventually. So do expect me to post something in the idea critique soon! I will also attempt to do a few critiques of other people's work if I feel confident.

My hobbies include nerdy things like playing video games and making video games (with Unity and RPGMaker), and occasionally writing fictions.

If I were an element, I'd probably be earth, because I am of calm, assertive and thoughtful nature, and I like to live my life steadily, with few unforeseen changes.

Thank you for reading and long live the Foundation!

item.title: Phantom Entry
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Emotional, Comedy, Mystery

Page Layout: Standard

Elevator Pitch: An SCP entry about an anomalous SCP entry.

Central Narrative: Out of nowhere, a new fully authorized SCP entry has appeared randomly in the Foundation's database, where it describes an entity so foreign and alien to the current local reality, where any and all sophisticated informational stimuli regarding it cannot be transcribed and comprehended when unaided, resulting in the immediate loss of said information after it removes its presence, such as memory. Translations, however, are perfectly comprehensible, such as written or recorded materials. However, it may also be corrupted if said entity acts upon it. The entity refers to itself in the English language as "Your Warden" or "Them", a being that proclaimed itself as the safe keeper of all reality from itself, by destroying realities beyond repair, and cleaning those near broken. However, even with all the SCP shenanigans, the time it spent observing the world(s) in this local reality had changed its mind, and coming to the absurd conclusion that the SCP universe may be the most convoluted, but it is far from broken, and everything belongs, resulting in its departure leaving this reality to its own business.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The mass confusion where absolutely no one remembers anything regarding the Security Containment Procedure ever transpiring adds to the curiosity of the reader, and it also enjoys the treatment of a drastic mood change, it slowly shifts from being a lighthearted slice of life reality hopping Mary Sue into a dreadful, cosmic horror-esque atmosphere. The horror will be mostly informational horror, the feeling of dread when presented absurd consensuses and information. There's just too much out there, and you have no say over it. The struggle to understand will lead to hatred, fear, confusion, denial, and much more will be explored.

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Greetings there, fellow SCP enthusiasts!

I am Seereeni (Seh-re-nii), and after roughly 5 years of knowing about and following the SCP universe, I decided to make an account of my own, and contribute to this wonderful place in whatever way I can.

One of mine own desires is to write an SCP, humanoid at that, which can then by used by everyone here, veteran and newbie, to link together all the SCPs, in one way or another, either for tales, to create new SCPs, to write interesting logs, or to explain something which they find hard to explain.

Hard? Oh yes, that's how a challenge should be.

I am also a writer on Fanfiction, as as far as my readers have commented, I am apparently almost typo-free in my writing. Do you have a tale or SCP you wish someone to look over for typos? Then do contact me, I am more than happy to help.

Lastly, as you have probably noticed, I am very…detailed in my explanations. This is, naturally, a good thing for a writer, but less so for an SCP Foundation member, something I am very much aware of. I have read the rules and I know that an SCP page should be professional and not use more words than needed. I will try my best to abide by these rules.

With that said, I still have a hard time understanding how this site works. So many links directing one to other links, then to other links…sigh. I barely know how Discord works.

Thus, to all of you veterans who have taken it upon themselves to answer newbie questions….I pity you, and I am sorry. I'll try to learn fast and keep your suffering minimal.

Kay bye.

item.title: SCP-6285 - The Putrefaction
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Action, Drama

Elevator Pitch:

+) It is a contagious fungus that is capable of raising the dead, then after a particular time, the now living dead will grow extra sharp bones out of their body, particularly the limbs. The reason being that having sharp "weapons" is the most useful way for SCP-6285-1 (The corpses) to kill other living humans which spreads the infection even further. The fungus shoots out spores and coming into contact with human corpses will begin to reanimate them. If there is a living human around there, it will attach to them as transportation without them knowing.

+) The unpredictable neverending evolution and mutation of the fungus is what makes it so deadly. This means SCP-6285-1 can have limitless potential and growth to serve the fungus's purpose.

+) SCP-6285-1 also has an invisible gooey substance which helps to patch its wounds if necessary. Using extreme heat is the best way to neutralize it.

Central Narrative: It should be from going normal, peaceful to a hell hole. At first, the SCP seems harmless and all, as time goes by, the horror and dreadfulness of it will soon come cause of how infectious it can spread and fast reanimation

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Putrefaction is unique in terms of reanimating the dead if this is a thing. To be honest, I was inspired by the Necromorphs in Dead Space to that the host growing extra limbs because it is the most helpful tactic to rank up more kills for the fungus to raise an army. The terrifying existence of the fungus can cause human extinction.

item.title: Re: {Seeking Greenlight} The Devil You Know
item.content:encoded:
Hi :)

+ Show
- Hope this helps :)

"demonic humanoid"

How is it demonic? What features make it demonic?

"indirectly through secondhand description"

How does the foundation contain this entity? How does the foundation ensure that reading the document doesn't cause its effects?

"pre-existing mental manipulative effects placed upon any human’s psyche."

what is considered a pre-existing mental effect?

"though anyone proven to acknowledge devil's existence from both direct or indirect sources can only be remedied with large doses of Class A amnestic"

I think mentioning that the entity has some correlation with the devil as besides the name and this sentence the closest that the entity is related to the devil is being called a demon. I think that this is focusing a lot on that the entity is a demon I think that putting descriptions of what it looks like and its ability. I think that focusing on showing that its a demon and not tell will help a lot (I said the meme) and its something to think about when you are writing the article

"The demon was borne out of an unknown man’s own sacrifice to ritualistically create something from the collective unconscious of humanity."

I like this as it creates the set up for this entity to be created on the idea of a man's efforts to create something to benefit humanity and it ultimately failing and creating something horrible I think that focusing on this could make for an interesting article

"Subject finds mild entertainment in playing with the strings of the human mind "

what is interesting to the entity? why does it like toying with the human mind? What is fun about it to them?

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
JamaisJ, can you elaborate a bit here to better help the author?

There's a lot of really cool things going on here,

Can you be more specific about what you liked here, and why? As an aside, the majority of the community isn't too keen on the typical overused "rage state" powers approach (that sort of formulaic setup has often been seen in low-rated articles that wound up quickly deleted).

but you need to pick a direction of some sort. There's no real narrative, just a lot of questions; solidify something in that regard.

What direction are you talking about here? Ongoing narrative involving the Foundation? Background context? Test logs with implications? What would you as a reader need to see solidified in order to be more interested in reading a draft of this material?

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
JamaisJ, can you explain your critique here to better help the author?

This is not a bad idea,

What about the concept did you like, and why? Is "not bad" good enough to convince you as a reader to be interested, or should the author try to edit this into something better?

but it needs some sort of specific manifestation, be it humanoid, item, or even a form of radiation. That lack of a specific manifestation is an issue.

Why is this an issue? There are plenty of articles about anomalous phenomena that don't have a physical manifestation that can't be empirically measured. Why does the author need to add this?

item.title: Re: People Seeds
item.content:encoded:
This is my first time in awhile doing this so here it goes

+ Show
- hope this helps :)

"A plant that unpredictably grows on unmarked or secluded graves."

What does this plant look like? What does it smell like? What does it feel like? I think that when writing this adding other senses other than sight will add more depth to your work

"land in a new place."

What is this new place? Is it supposed to be a dead body? If so please clarify.

"The plant matures into a baby with the exact genetic makeup of the deceased."

How does the plant do this? Is the baby a plant or an animal? How does the plant reproduce? What happens when a person dies? Does it create another instance of this SCP? or does it just die like a human? Do the clones behave differently than a regular person? Can they spread the spores too? How fast do the clones mature? Are the clones really human or is it just an appearance?

"resurrecting and scattering hundreds of them across the nation."

How does this happen? How does the rogue pull this off? What hoops did the rouge do to pull this off? Why so many bodies?

"Foundation to track down and contain the clones of the people they killed"

What struggles does the foundation go through to find them? What takes them so long? What are the consequences if they don't find them?

"Evidence begins to show that a guilty rogue researcher may have planted the SCP deliberately to resurrect a D-class they were attached to."

Why were they attached to the D class? Are they also "looking" for the clones? Where do they come in throughout the story? How are you going to showcase the search? with exploration logs? What are the consequences of his actions?

Overall I enjoy the idea of someone the SCP but I think some more in this details will help
